# Open questions

*Generated by `build/gen_open_questions.py` from `docs/open-questions/`, one file
per question. **Edit the question's own file, never this index** — the next run
overwrites it. The register's own history, including the four id-collision
conversion tables, is in [`docs/open-questions/README.md`](open-questions/README.md).*

**Two namespaces, and the second cannot collide.** Entries 1-99 keep their numbers
forever; every question raised after 28 August 2026 is NAMED `oq/<slug>` and lives in
`docs/open-questions/oq-<slug>.md`. A number has to be issued from somewhere, and the
only shared state two parallel sessions have is the repository they both branched
from -- so both read the highest number in their own copy and whoever merges second
renumbers, which happened FIVE times in four days. A slug is derived from its subject
rather than issued, so two sessions that pick the same one have raised the same
question and get the add/add conflict they should get. `build/check_ids.py` refuses a
numbered file above 99 and `build/check_citations.py` refuses a numbered entry above
it, so the mechanism that collided five times is unavailable rather than discouraged.

Decisions deferred rather than made quietly. Two of these came from authoring the
Georgian kit end to end, which was the point of doing it.

**137 questions, of which 53 are open.** A question is OPEN while
it awaits a ruling; the two HALF CLOSED entries count as open, because a half-closed
question is an open one. Status words in use, and no others —
**open:** `OPEN`, `STILL OPEN`, `HALF CLOSED`, `PARTLY`, `IN PROGRESS`;
**settled:** `CLOSED`, `RESOLVED`, `RULED`, `FIXED`, `CONFIRMED`, `ANSWERED`, `LEFT AS A STANDING DISCLOSURE`, `SUPERSEDED`, `WITHDRAWN`.
`build/check_ids.py` fails the build on any other word rather than assuming it benign.

| **28** | FIXED 24 AUG 2026 | [`build/modcache.py`, one process-wide cache keyed by real path; every local `_mod()`/`_load()` now delegates to it. Steady-state `check()` 3.06 s → 0.31 s, `compose()` 30-40 s → 7-9 s, the full 291-test suite 3 chunks / ~12 min → one run / 2 min 24 s, restoring WP-0.3's "under five minutes" acceptance line. The profile turned out to understate the problem: a *single* `check()` was executing plan_check 16 times, geometry 8, structure 4, and roof/core/elevation/proportion_engine twice each, because the by-path loads are module-level and nest (elevation → plan_check + geometry + structure + roof + engine; roof → plan_check + geometry + structure; structure → plan_check + geometry; geometry → plan_check), so the whole tree was re-walked at every entry point rather than only `core._data()` going cold. Neither of the two fixes proposed below was taken: caching `core` at `plan_check`'s scope would have fixed one edge of that graph and left the other fifteen loads in place, and an mtime-keyed disk cache would have added a staleness class this corpus does not otherwise have. The delegation approach keeps the by-path convention exactly as it was — every script still runs standalone, every call site keeps its signature — and only stops the re-execution. Pinned by `tests/test_modcache.py` (5 tests, including a counter asserting a warm `check()` executes no module at all). The one behavioural change: a cached module is not re-executed, so a process that mutates a corpus file and re-loads in-process will not see the change — safe here because the mutation tests in `test_ontology.py`/`test_constraints.py` all run their checker as a subprocess, and `modcache.invalidate()` exists for anything that ever needs it. See `docs/reports/oq-28-module-cache.md`](open-questions/028-build-modcache-py-process-wide-cache-keyed-real-path.md) |
